asking.note: Page opened. 9ct rose gold open-circle brooch, 3 seed pearls and red paste stone, c.1900-1910, 2.1g. Only the pre-sale estimate is visible, so this is an estimate, not a price paid. aud_price is the midpoint.

lots.guide_summary: Five close SOLD results (four Denhams UK 2026, one Noble Sydney Nov 2025) run A$85 to A$380 per single brooch or small pair; one Australian auction estimate A$140-240 (ASKING). No UNSOLD. Nothing found for a 'Mother' script brooch specifically. Combining one bar brooch and one damaged brooch, the UK evidence suggests about A$200 to A$390 for this pair. GBP at 1.8983 AUD (open.er-api.com, 14 Oct 2026). Melt note only: 9ct A$71.53/g (metalcharts.org, 14 Oct 2026), so 7.4g gross would be about A$529 if all gold, but stones, pearls and a likely base-metal hinge mean less; melt is a floor reference, not a sale.
lots.working: No exact same-item sale (a pair), so the keep figure adds the lowest close sale for each piece: bar brooch A$114 (Denhams lot 38) + damaged brooch A$85 (Denhams lot 71) = A$199; 199 / 1.198 = 166.1, rounded down to $165. Flip: likely resale about A$260 (bar brooch median about A$142 plus damaged script brooch about A$85-110, plus extra weight), less eBay-type fees about 13.4% (A$35) and A$12 postage = A$213; 213 / 2.396 = 88.9, rounded down to $85. Badgers (Aug 2024) excluded as over 24 months. Kalmar and metalcharts entries dropped as not prices paid.
lots.confidence_reason: Mother brooch shows an anchor and a 9-type mark (Birmingham 9ct likely); bar brooch marks are only partly legible. Several close SOLD pages opened, but none is the same pair and most are UK.
lots.dropped_entries: Kalmar Antiques turquoise brooch: dropped, page shows '$Sold' with no price; 'less than $500' is marketing copy, not a price. metalcharts.org melt: moved to the note, melt is not a sale or asking price. Moorabool moved from a value to an estimate-only ASKING entry (unchanged kind). Badgers kept only as an out-of-window category guide.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: Mother brooch with several empty pearl settings and a bent tail; bar brooch intact with red stone and two pearl trefoils. Photo 2 (enlarged): three small struck marks on the bar brooch back, worn and not clearly legible as 9ct. Photo 3 (cropped): Mother brooch has anchor, '9'-type and a third mark consistent with Birmingham 9ct; the hinge/pin assembly looks grey, likely base metal.
lots.condition: Bar brooch appears complete. Mother brooch has missing pearls, a bent tail and a probably non-gold hinge; repair or sale for weight.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are both brooches marked 9ct (the bar brooch marks are hard to read)? Is the Mother brooch hinge/pin gold or base metal, and how many pearls are missing? Is the 7.4g for both brooches together?

lots.guide_summary: All seven surviving entries are SOLD (Denhams UK, Feb 2025 to Sep 2026), A$190 to A$304; no UNSOLD or ASKING survives. No Australian auction result with a visible price was found. 2026 sales of 4-5g 9ct signets cluster at £130-160 (A$247-304). GBP at 1.8983 AUD (open.er-api.com, 14 Oct 2026). Melt note only: 4.6g x A$71.53/g = about A$329 (metalcharts.org, 14 Oct 2026), a floor reference, not a sale.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in 24 months = A$190 (Denhams Feb 2025, 4.6g); 190 / 1.198 = 158.6, rounded down to $155. Flip: likely resale about A$250 (2026 median about A$275, discounted for the shoulder split), less eBay-type fees about 13.4% (A$34) and A$12 postage = A$204; 204 / 2.396 = 85.1, rounded down to $85.
lots.confidence_reason: 9ct mark read in photo 2 and several matching SOLD pages opened, but all are UK and the shoulder split lowers condition versus the comps.
lots.dropped_entries: eBay AU asking AU$195-750: dropped, snippet only and eBay is closed to us. Kalmar Antiques 1937 signet: dropped, sold with no price shown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2: '9CT' stamp clearly legible inside the shank. Photo 1 (enlarged): heavy surface wear, monogram almost worn away, and a visible split running through the right shoulder, not just a scratch.
lots.condition: Worn, monogram largely gone, apparent crack or split on one shoulder; may need repair before wearing.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the line on the right shoulder a crack or split (or an old solder join)? Please confirm weight 4.6g and size W.

lots.what_it_is: Bag of 7 gold-tone wristwatches: gold-plated Omega De Ville Quartz square head (no strap), round gold-plated Omega quartz date with company logo dial on worn strap, gold-tone Seiko automatic day-date, a rolled-gold cushion watch with crazed dial, and three small ladies watches. Running state unknown.

sold.note: Page opened. Single Omega De Ville Quartz 192.0034, c.1978, gold-plated cushion case, white Roman dial, ticking but needs service. Similar to our square De Ville head, but undated so cannot set a max. Rate 1.6039 AUD/EUR.

Page opened. Two watches: vintage manual Omega in round gold-tone case (page also says '14C', so it may be 14k gold, not plated) and a Seiko 7A34 chronograph. Untested. Different watches to ours. Rate 1.4328 AUD/USD.

Page opened. Gents Omega Automatic Seamaster, cal 501, gilt metal case, running, no strap. Shows a plated vintage Omega can make good money, but an automatic Seamaster is more sought after than a 1970s-80s quartz De Ville. Rate 1.8983.
Page opened. Two Rotary quartz and a Mappin & Webb in gilt cases. Guide for the minor gold-tone watches only.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: square Omega head reads 'De Ville Quartz' with date, gold baton dial, no strap. Round Omega with date has a company logo on the dial, which usually lowers collector value. Seiko automatic day-date with worn dial on a two-tone bracelet. Cushion watch has a badly crazed dial. lots.question_for_gowans: Do any of the watches run (especially the two Omegas and the Seiko)? Do the Omega case backs show genuine Omega references and are the movements present? Is the cushion watch rolled gold or solid gold?
